briefs.label: Carapace crawler (one shared spider-type rig)
briefs.why: A low, wide, many-legged body on a rig shared with another creature family makes a readable hazard on a phone screen. Silhouette is the hook: flat shell, short legs, fast scuttle.
keep: one rig reused across two families
change: shell plates replaced by a spiked ridge in a different colour
two extra legs and a split tail, not the donor proportions
a burrow-up attack instead of a plain walk-in

briefs.label: Winged stone guardian (rig shared with a small winged imp)
briefs.why: Stone wings on a humanoid body read as a patient guard. The mood is still and heavy until it moves.
keep: a rig shared with a second, smaller family
change: two jagged wings instead of a bat-like spread
an ember core in the chest as the threat colour
a wing-snap telegraph before the lunge

briefs.label: Horned brute (bull-headed, heavy, chain belt)
briefs.why: A head-first silhouette with a wide horn span reads from 375 px wide and gives a clear charge tell.
keep: horned bull head as the readable top
a shared rig with a second brute family
change: antler-like horn spread instead of two curved horns
chain belt as a second silhouette feature
a stomp with a dust ring instead of a bellow

briefs.label: Dragon family on one body (several colour and ornament variants)
briefs.why: One dragon rig carried through many variants gives a whole tier of bosses from one animation set. The idea is the family, not any one dragon.
keep: one rig for a family of dragons
scale and ornament as the per-variant levers
a dedicated header per variant in the data file
change: each variant gets its own wing shape, not a palette swap
head ornaments replaced by a crown of crystal shards
a per-variant breath or aura effect in our own colours

inspiration: Family-level rig sharing: each row of the animation source table pairs a family with a shared rig code, so several creatures ride one animation set. Recreate as a family table with a rig id and a body id, not as copies of any one creature.
One humanoid rig, many bodies: the table lists male and female codes that share one rig, so body variants differ in mesh while animation stays the same. Useful for our hero and NPC variants.

Sound and music instances placed as zone data: the README feature list (lines 17-22) names music and sound instances inside zone data, and SoundConstants.cs uses EMIT and LOOP emission types (lines 5-6). Recreate as ambience emitters in zone data with an emit-once or loop flag.

Binary sound bank with fixed-size entries: EffSounds.cs line 10 says the bank is binary and fixed-length per entry (the size check is at line 47). Our sound pipeline can use a flat, indexed bank for fast load on phones.

Vertex-colour lighting baked into zone meshes (README line 17 'Vertex colors', line 18 'BSP tree', line 19 'Ambient light'): a cheap lit look with no runtime light cost. Worth a look for the 375 px target.
Collision separate from visuals, with hidden boundary geometry exported on request (settings.txt lines 25-27, ExportHiddenGeometry). Keep invisible walls as data, not as drawn meshes.
Region-split zone mesh (settings.txt lines 17-19, ExportZoneMeshGroups): zones split into region meshes so the client can stream or cull by region. Matches our zone streaming problem.
